hook: A halide pretreatment anchors the molecular layer in perovskite solar cells, reaching 27.3% efficiency.
summary: The authors find that buried interfaces fail by adhesion loss under temperature swings, and treat the transparent oxide with a metal halide so the self-assembled monolayer binds at many points. Devices reach 27.3 percent efficiency (26.9 certified) and keep 94 percent after 400 cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C. Only small lab cells were tested, and long-term outdoor durability is not shown.
title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
